sections.html:
Caldwell County is foothills country in the state's northwest, with Lenoir as its seat. Population was estimated at 81,105 on July 1, 2025, living in 38,057 housing units. Owners occupy 73.5% of the homes, and the 2020-2024 middle value for an owned home is $192,200.

Nine municipalities touch the county: Lenoir, Hudson, Granite Falls, Cedar Rock, Cajahs Mountain, Gamewell, Sawmills, and parts of Blowing Rock and Rhodhiss. The town your parcel falls in changes the bill, since each one sets its own rate and a couple set none.

The Tax Office is at 905 West Avenue NW, Lenoir, NC 28645. Hours run 8 to 5 on weekdays, with weekends and federal holidays off. By mail, write to PO Box 2200, Lenoir, NC 28645. The main number is 828-757-1340, and listing questions can go to 828-757-1320.

The office lists personal property and business property, bills and collects the tax, and runs revaluation. For a home sale you care about three things: the assessed value of the real estate, whether any year's bill is delinquent, and whether the owner is enrolled in a relief program. The county advertises tax liens on real property once bills go unpaid, and the commissioners authorized advertising of 2024 liens at their February 2025 meeting.

Bills are due September 1. After that, a bill still unpaid on January 6 of the next year picks up 2 percent interest, and three-fourths of a percent more for every month it stays open. Timeliness is judged by the U.S. Postal Service postmark, and postage-meter dates are refused.

Practical points on paying:

  • You may pay part of the bill any time between its arrival and January 6.
  • Online payment takes American Express, Discover, Mastercard, Visa or a PayPal account, and PayPal's processing fees are not kept by the county.
  • Escrow does not redirect the bill away from you. If your lender should be paying it, ask the lender.
  • Personal property bills such as boats and unlicensed vehicles are mailed in July.

The 2026 rate chart also shows a discount of 2.00 for July and 1.00 for August. G.S. 105-360 lets a county adopt a prepayment discount schedule approved by the Department of Revenue, so ask the Tax Office how the discount is applied before you count on it.

The county rate for 2026 is 0.4666, and a town or district adds its own line. Rates are quoted per $100 of assessed value. Lenoir is 0.4600, with a separate downtown district at 0.1800, and fire and rescue districts add further lines for rural parcels.

A household solid waste fee of 22.75 applies, or 17.75 for city households. Rural fire districts run from 0.0430 for Bethlehem to 0.1415 for South Caldwell, so the district your house sits in changes the bill. The Tax Office can tell you which fire and rescue districts include your parcel.

Caldwell County reappraised all real property for 2025, after its sales-assessment ratio fell below the 0.85 level that triggers a reappraisal under state law. The prior revaluation took effect January 1, 2021. The point of a reappraisal is to give every taxpayer equal, uniform values.

County staff appraised residential property, and a third party handled commercial and industrial property. Many owners saw large jumps in assessed value, and commissioners talked about cutting the rate toward revenue neutral. If you plan to sell, compare the assessed value on your bill with what buyers are offering.

State law sets an eight-year outer limit under G.S. 105-286. A county of 75,000 residents or more must move up its reappraisal if the sales ratio slips under .85 or climbs over 1.15, which is what happened here.

Begin with the informal review. The Board of Equalization and Review hears a case only after that step. Return the Informal Review Form, and back it with a recent fee appraisal tied to local sales, or a comparison of similar homes by year built, size, construction and acreage. The county advises against paying for an independent appraisal unless you truly need one.

The Board of Equalization and Review is the formal body, and anyone still unhappy after it can go to the NC Property Tax Commission. Under G.S. 105-322, the board first meets between early April and early May, and your hearing request has to reach it before it adjourns. The Caldwell board has five members and four alternates, who must have lived in the county at least two years.

Personal property is separate. Appeals of individual or business personal property values go in writing to the Caldwell County Assessor's Office, PO Box 2200, Lenoir, NC 28645, within 30 days of the tax bill date. Business listings that miss the January 31 deadline without an approved extension carry a 10 percent penalty on the total tax.

Caldwell County follows the state's three programs, and the county tax site has a relief brochure and an application. Elderly or disabled owners can use the exclusion in G.S. 105-277.1 which shelters the larger of $25,000 or 50 percent of a home's appraised value. The 2026 income cap is $38,800.

A separate disabled veteran exclusion removes the first $45,000 of appraised value. The circuit breaker caps tax at 4.0 or 5.0 percent of income, with a 2026 upper threshold of $58,200. Form AV-9 is the application, filed with the county assessor. The county must accept it through June 1 ahead of the tax year. Owners cannot combine the three programs.

If you own improvements, report new buildings and additions during January, with your cost and the percent complete on January 1. Report demolished improvements too.

sections.h2: Selling with the tax bill still open
sections.html:
The bill goes to whoever owned the property on January 1. If you closed after that date, pass the bill to the buyer. The lien attaches as of January 1 under G.S. 105-355, so the closing attorney should settle the current year and any open prior years.

Get a written payoff from the Tax Office, and look at which town or fire district appears on the bill, since the combined charge differs from parcel to parcel. If the house was inherited or has back years unpaid, get the full list of open years before you accept an offer. Delinquent taxes are collected through foreclosure. A cash sale has no lender payoff to coordinate, though the tax lien still gets cleared at the closing table.

faqs.q: When are Caldwell County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1 of the tax year. Interest begins January 6 of the following year at 2 percent, then three-fourths of one percent a month until paid, and the county uses the U.S. Postal postmark, not a meter date.

faqs.q: Where do I pay or ask about my Caldwell County tax bill?
faqs.a: Go to 905 West Avenue NW in Lenoir any weekday from 8 to 5, or phone 828-757-1340. Online payment works by credit card or PayPal, and the processing fees go to PayPal rather than the county.

faqs.q: When did Caldwell County last revalue property?
faqs.a: The county reappraised real property for 2025, and before that a revaluation took effect on January 1, 2021. State law caps the gap at eight years, and a low sales ratio of under .85 can force it sooner.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Caldwell County real estate value?
faqs.a: Return the informal review form with comparable sales or an appraisal. If you disagree with the result, request a hearing from the Board of Equalization and Review before it adjourns. From there the NC Property Tax Commission takes appeals filed within 30 days of the mailed board decision.

faqs.q: If I sold my Caldwell County house after January 1, who gets the bill?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is billed, so forward a copy to the buyer. The county tries to notify the new owner but asks sellers to help.
